subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should the public Plugin SDK expose durable transient storage, and if so should its permanent identity and lifecycle be plugin-global, agent-scoped, or explicitly support both scopes?
rationale: Current main contains relevant SQLite primitives, but source and policy do not decide whether untrusted installed plugins may access agent databases or what compatibility and security guarantees that public API must provide.

options.title: Define one scoped storage API
options.body: Specify explicit plugin-global and/or agent-scoped namespaces, trust rules, TTL, quotas, cleanup, and migration behavior before implementing the SDK surface.

options.title: Keep storage plugin-owned
options.body: Retain the trusted internal store and require external plugins to manage their own SQLite state until a concrete missing SDK capability is demonstrated.

options.title: Decline generic cache storage
options.body: Close the direction unless a named plugin and reproducible restart-loss case establishes a sufficiently general core API need.

recommendation.title: Define one scoped storage API
recommendation.body: Specify explicit plugin-global and/or agent-scoped namespaces, trust rules, TTL, quotas, cleanup, and migration behavior before implementing the SDK surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin-state SQLite work makes this the closest available owner for choosing whether the existing store should become a supported external SDK contract.
